End of Abyss: Explore and Fight Through the Abyss’ Horror
From our small studio Section 9 Interactive, founded by three former Tarsier Studios members, comes the sci-fi action adventure game End of Abyss , launching October 1 for XBOX Series X|S players!
In End of Abyss , you take on the role of a young combat technician, Cel, as she and her crew venture down into a large broken down facility under ground. You will face threats lurking, upgrade Cel’s gear and find the tools you need to go further into the facility.
Taking this game from a prototype to a finished game has been a long time in the making. What started as an action-based top-down shooter, developed into a slower, more dynamic and atmospheric experience as we became more interested in exploration and creating a stronger sense of tension.
Along the way, we realized that we had not really seen very many top-down metroidvania games with action horror elements. That idea became our driving force and eventually helped shape the game into what it is today.
While early versions of End of Abyss had much of the character’s basic movement and equipment, some enemies with basic destruction, as well as some small levels, it didn’t have a clear focus when it came to its visual identity. Once we became more interested in an atmospheric and eerie experience, we discussed references, sketched our ideas and developed updated prototype enemies and environments to try to find the look that we found most interesting.
The inspiration behind the game’s atmosphere and art stems from the films, games, comic books and anime that we grew up with. The media created around the 1980s and 1990s was usually a bit rough and had some manually created effects in video and sounds, which gave them a certain weathered look and feel. We wanted to bring some of that into the facility in End of Abyss to develop a world that feels worn down and slightly awkward, and to make the player feel uneasy about the environment around them. At the same time, we still wanted it to look like a brand new world, so we balanced realism with a slightly stylised sense of scale and shapes in the world, as well as the creatures that reside in it.
Our workflow for creating enemies has been to first come up with gameplay functions that we would like to try out, and then try to find a fitting type of creature design that would emphasize those ideas. Sketching a lot of these concepts and getting fast, rough animation mockups and enemy prototypes running in Unreal was key to developing the variety of enemies and bosses in the game. We ended up creating a lot of mockups for enemy animations, their behaviors, as well as their destruction.

packages.headline: Microsoft Jewel Comes to Mobile with XBOX Achievements and Game Pass Benefits

sources.label: Xbox Wire
sources.evidenceText:
Microsoft Jewel is the fifth mobile game from Microsoft Casual Games – the team’s first new mobile launch in seven years – with XBOX Achievements and progress that syncs across mobile and PC.
Microsoft Jewel Comes to Mobile with XBOX Achievements and Game Pass Benefits
For the first time in seven years, Microsoft Casual Games has launched a new mobile app – Microsoft Jewel is available now as a standalone app for iOS and Android. It becomes the fifth app in the Microsoft Casual Games mobile lineup.
The launch gives players a new way to enjoy a familiar Match-3 favorite, earn XBOX Achievements on mobile, and keep their progress connected across mobile and PC.
If you’ve played Microsoft Jewel on PC, in Microsoft Solitaire Collection , or through the XBOX mobile app, the gameplay will feel familiar. Match three or more jewels to clear them from the board, build your score, and make room for your next move. It’s easy to jump in for a few minutes, with plenty of opportunities to keep playing when you have more time.
At the heart of Microsoft Jewel is the simple satisfaction of finding the right match. Each move can open new possibilities across the board. Create Bonus Jewels, place them where they will have the biggest impact, and use power-ups to set off chain reactions.
Microsoft Jewel also gives players a new way to earn XBOX Achievements from a mobile device. Sign in with a Microsoft account to track your accomplishments and keep building your Xbox profile wherever you play.
Sign in with a Microsoft account to sync your progress between Microsoft Jewel on iOS, Android, and the standalone PC app. Play on your phone while you’re away from your computer, then return to the PC version without starting over.
XBOX Game Pass members receive Premium benefits when playing Microsoft Jewel on PC, including an ad-free experience and additional in-game benefits. XBOX Game Pass Ultimate members receive those Premium benefits on both PC and mobile.

packages.headline: PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for October: F1 25, Hunt: Showdown 1896, Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2

sources.label: PlayStation Blog
sources.evidenceText:
All playable from October 6.
PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for October: F1 25, Hunt: Showdown 1896, Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2
Race for podium glory in F1 25, take on monsters and other players in Hunt: Showdown 1896, then battle voxel versions of EDF enemies in Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2. Together, these three games form the PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for October. All be available to PlayStation Plus members* from Tuesday October 6 until Monday November 2.
Let’s take a closer look at each of the games.
Leave your mark on the world of racing in F1 25, the official video game of the 2025 FIA Formula One World Championship. Enjoy single player experiences such as Career and My Team 2.0, letting you create your own F1 stories as you take control as the Owner of a Formula 1 team. Then take the race online against other players, including a brand new multiplayer mode in F1 World, where you and your friends race as a squad against AI drivers.
Hunt: Showdown 1896 | PS5 
Hunt: Showdown 1896 is a new era of the addictively unforgiving extraction shooter. In corrupted backwaters lost to history, fight back alone – or with friends – against timeless evil. Twisted monsters and other ruthless Hunters stand between you and your Bounty. Risk everything as Hunt consumes you. Race competing Hunters to track down bosses, send them to hell, claim their bounty, and fight your way to extract. If others only slow you down, go alone. If you find strength in numbers, take up to two teammates along.
Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2 | PS5, PS4
The square Earth is under attack by giant enemies. Teammates scattered around the world are waiting to be rescued. Select 4 teammates from among those you have collected and create your own team. Design the team perfect for your play style, select your equipment, and then deploy to battle. In addition to soldiers from the mainline EDF series, this game also includes soldiers from the EDF spin-offs, and enemies who ravaged the planet in previous releases have also crossed over into this world to join the fight. Enjoy fighting numerous enemies, including redesigned voxel versions of old favorites, as well as new enemies unique to this release. Enjoy four player online co-op and two player local split screen on PS5 and PS4.

『残クレバハムートで魔王討伐 ──10億Gの相棒と、月々10万Gの冒険。』は、ファンタジーADVだ。主人公は、平和な日常を送っていた青年レオン。ある日、神様から魔王討伐の任務を任され、その相棒として強力な竜「バハムート」を貸し出される。

Crimson Desert Charting the Unknown Expansion Delayed Two Weeks
Crimson Desert's first expansion was only just announced at the State of Play in September with a very ambitious October 15 release date. Unfortunately, it seems that target was a little too ambitious.
Pearl Abyss announced that the Charting the Unknown expansion would be delayed by two weeks, in order to "deliver a more polished and stable gameplay experience." But even with this delay, the new expansion is coming remarkably close to the game's initial release, and hopefully the developer will have even more content planned for the future.
The expansion comes just seven months after Crimson Desert intially released back on March 19. And while the reception to the game was mixed, a lot of its initial issues have since been ironed out, turning the game into one of the breakout hits of the year.
Hello, Greymanes. We would like to share an update regarding Crimson Desert’s upcoming DLC. pic.twitter.com/mKNmYn10jX
This first expansion will expand the game to a new zone, and will bring sea exploration to the already expansive world. Charting the unknown will also bring more robust base building, with the trailer suggesting you'll be able to actually build new buildings, which will only add another hundred hours to my play time.
Crimson Desert's Charting the Unknown expansion will now launch on October 29, and will set you back $24.99. And just like the base game, it'll be available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and PC.

packages.headline: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered Review Update

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
The best this already amazing RPG has ever been.
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered Review Update
As the fantasy RPG GOAT, it really doesn’t take a whole lot for me to replay The Witcher 3. I’ve happily done so the numerous other times developer CD Projekt Red has revamped this masterpiece, but The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered seems to be the biggest overhaul to the beloved tale yet. A free update for anyone who owns the original, so many different parts of this already excellent game have been improved – from combat to movement to skill progression (not to mention the modernized graphics). After about 10 hours working my way through White Orchard and beyond, it’s already extremely clear that this is the best The Witcher 3 has ever been.
It’s probably not controversial to say that one of the worst parts of this otherwise amazing adventure was the combat. Even after at least a few updates to it over the years, it still mostly felt floaty, a bit on the sloppy side, and enemies were a huge fan of just standing there and waiting for their turn to get decapitated. The modernizations made to combat in this remaster are its biggest step forward, as a whole bevy of tweaks have been made to address various sticking points. Geralt attacks faster and enemies are quicker to match your pace, which makes the process of chopping through your ninth pack of wolves much less irritating.
The camera and lock-on functionality have been the highlight so far, as you can now toggle between large groups of enemies with ease, and without the camera losing its mind. I didn’t even use the lock-on system in the original specifically because it was so unreliable, so being able to do so now has taken some serious getting used to. In general, the camera feels much better – less tightly locked to your back so you can handle groups of enemies more reliably (though those darn Neckers still like to sneak up on ya), and so far I’ve encountered far fewer situations where I felt like I was fighting my view as much as I was the monsters.
I’ve also noticed some new enemy behaviors that make swordplay more interesting, specifically how they’ll now retreat instead of letting you trounce them with steel, launch less telegraphed counterattacks, and disappear and reappear behind you (in the case of ghost monsters). All that did a much better job of making me feel like I was fighting intelligent creatures. Of course, compared to some of the stuff we see in action games today, I still do feel like the enemy behavior shows its age, and it was never all that great to begin with. Still, this is enough of an improvement to make combat feel much more engaging than it once did, significantly upgrading one of this adventure’s weakest points.
Movement is one of those small details that can grate the heck out of you in a massive RPG like The Witcher 3, slowly filling you with rage over the course of hundreds of hours. In the original, Geralt was often slow and had a lot of trouble getting over things. His rigid animations sometimes made me avoid ladders altogether because I just didn’t have the patience for it. In the remaster, Geralt absolutely flies over fences and navigates vertical obstacles with relative ease, to the point where it actually felt weird to see him be so nimble. I recall losing over an hour of progress in the 1.0 version when Geralt fell off a ledge no taller than a barstool and managed to break every bone in his body. This was reduced already in the next-gen update from 2022, but combined with the other speed and mobility improvements here, it almost feels like a completely different game – to the point where I’ve begun to wonder if it’ll make the map feel smaller than before as I get deeper in.
Similarly, Roach is no longer the annoying idiot she once was, now sporting much more intuitive controls that make her less likely to get caught on trees (which she now passes through if she’s just brushing against them while galloping), or end up on top of a barn. Mo

packages.headline: Ubisoft Montreal employees launch collective action to preserve hybrid work schedule

sources.label: Game Developer
sources.evidenceText:
Workers at Ubisoft Montreal are taking collective action to protect their hybrid work schedule.
Ubisoft Montreal employees launch collective action to preserve hybrid work schedule
Ubisoft Montreal workers in the Ubisoft Workers of Montreal union have started a petition "to preserve hybrid work," according to a statement posted on GWU Montreal social media . As of Wednesday, the petition has reached more than 300 signatures from Ubisoft employees . Many of the signatures were collected in person, GWU Montreal said.
"Today marks the public launch of the Ubisoft Workers of Montreal (UWM) campaign, with a first action: a petition to preserve hybrid work," GWU posted. "Every Ubisoft Montreal employee is invited to sign the petition and every supporter encouraged to reach out to their network to encourage them to sign!"
Ubisoft announced in January that it was calling all employees to return to the office five days per week. It also said it was enacting layoffs, delays, and studio closures. Ubisoft, at that time, had just secured a $1.25 billion investment from Tencent. The "rightsizing" was intended to "reclaim [Ubisoft's] creative leadership, regain agility and drive sharp rebound." Ubisoft said in its January press release that the return to office policy was intended to encourage collaboration.
Ubisoft's Paris-based employees went on strike shortly after the announcement to protest the policy.
When Ubisoft Montreal team lead David Michaud-Cromp commented publicly on the policy— suggesting there may be another reason other than productivity for the layoffs —Ubisoft put the veteran employee on unpaid leave. He was fired a week later. Ubisoft said in a statement to Game Developer that "sharing feedback or opinions respectfully does not lead to a dismissal."
It continued: "We have a clear Code of Conduct that outlines our shared expectations for working together safely and respectfully, which employees review and sign each year. When that is breached, our established procedures apply, including an escalation of measures depending on the nature, severity and repetition of the breach."
GWU Montreal is instructing Ubisoft workers interested in signing the petition to do so in person by "meet[ing] your colleagues during [break] hours".
A petition is the first action.

packages.headline: 'We Have Been Gradually Preparing': Capcom Already Has a Plan for When Its Resident Evil Remakes Catch Up With Newer Games

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Capcom has a plan for when its rollout of Resident Evil remakes eventually catches up with newer games in the series, and considers Resident Evil 7 as a "turning point."
'We Have Been Gradually Preparing': Capcom Already Has a Plan for When Its Resident Evil Remakes Catch Up With Newer Games
That's according to Jun Takeuchi, a Capcom veteran who has served as excutive producer for the series over the past decade, who has acknowledged the fact that Capcom's hugely popular remakes are slowly running out of classic games to re-release. The publisher has already remade Resident Evil 2, 3 and 4 to great success, with a new version of Code Veronica slated for next year.
It has previously been reported that a Resident Evil 0 remake will follow in 2028, and that a Resident Evil 1 remake has also been considered. Of the mainline Resident Evil games, this would then just leave Resident Evil 5 and 6 as the only titles left to get new versions — both of which would be interesting prospects, for separate reasons.
While Capcom likely has enough remakes to keep their releases going for another decade, there will come a point where the publisher needs to decide whether to remake other titles, or start remaking its remakes all over again. Or... do something else, Takeuchi teased.
"Someday, the remake series will catch up with the era of the numbered titles, and we are already thinking about what we will do when that happens," he continued. "In fact, we have been gradually preparing for that since around Resident Evil Village. The appearance of names such as Umbrella and Spencer, as well as the return of Raccoon City in Requiem, are also in preparation for a 'crossover'.
Takeuchi went on to state that Capcom regarded Resident Evil 7 "as a turning point for the series" as it was in development when its plans to start remaking older games really came to fruition. Does this mean that everything before 7 is set to be remade one day, while 7 and onwards is considered too new?
Resident Evil 5 sold hugely well, with particular interest in the game in the wake of the top-rated Resident Evil 4. (Sadly, 5 was nowhere near as good.) But any new version of the game would see Capcom returning to the controversy over 5's African setting and companion character Sheva. As for Resident Evil 6, which featured a range of protagonists, it just isn't very good. But perhaps Capcom could salvage it in an eventual new version?
"We regard '7' as a turning point."

packages.headline: "Extraction is Still a Major Part of Marathon" – Marathon Game Director Reassures Fans Main Game Mode Isn't Going Anywhere

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Just last week, Marathon's developers laid out a new roadmap for the game that'd bring PvE and deathmatch modes to the game, but now Game Director Del Chafe has reassured fans that the extraction mode will not be sunsetted.
"Extraction is Still a Major Part of Marathon" – Marathon Game Director Reassures Fans Main Game Mode Isn't Going Anywhere
When Bungie revealed the roadmap last week , some people were worried that the more hardcore extraction mode would be neglected in favor of the new modes, especially after the developer admitted that Marathon flopped because it was too hard . But, using the Marathon Development Team Twitter account, Chafe reassured folks, saying "We want to be clear, Extraction is still a major part of Marathon, and we're also going to continue updating it as we look to the future of the game."
Hey everyone, Del here. Last week we had a great time talking about the upcoming PvE and experimental PvP modes for Symbiosis in December. We want to be clear, Extraction is still a major part of Marathon, and we're also going to continue updating it as we look to the future…
Chafe also asked fans for feedback, saying "We'd love to hear from you on what you're enjoying about Extraction today, what you think needs work, and what you wish was there." Of course, Marathon fans obliged.
Marathon streamer Drewsky replied , saying that the among the main problems facing the extraction mode are spawn rushes and harsh death spirals that price players out. User nsorrey36 echoed Drewsky, saying "Echoing a lot of sentiment where it feels like lobby wiping is the go-to strategy of the run."
It seems like the perfect solution to Marathon's problems would be to introduce the new game modes coming in the Symbiosis update, while also finding a way to incentivize extraction players to not immediately start running for spawn points in the hopes of catching someone off guard. Luckily, it sounds like Bungie is taking any and all community feedback to heart, so there's actually a chance that extraction will look a lot different in a year.
All of these changes for Marathon are happening at the same time that Bungie is working on bringing Destiny back. The developer reassured gamers earlier this month that it wasn't done with Destiny , and is working on bringing back vaulted Destiny 2 content.

先日弊誌で取り上げた、「ひきこもりリスク」とゲーム内での「交流の好み」の関係を調査した論文の執筆者のひとりにインタビューを実施した。
“ひきこもりリスク”とゲーム内での“交流の好み”の関係を調査した「ゲーム研究者」にインタビュー。「一人になりたい」と想う背景は？キャラとの“思い出”にはどんな意味がある？色々訊いてみた
今年7月、奈良先端科学技術大学院大学などの研究チームが「日本のゲーマーにおける社会的周縁化リスクと社会的交流傾向の負の関連性（Social marginalization risk and its negative association with socialising preferences in Japanese gamers）」と題する論文を 発表した （以下、論文A）。この論文Aは、社会的に孤立しうるリスク（社会的周縁化リスク）と、ゲーム内行動の嗜好との関係を統計的に分析したものだ。結果として、社会的に孤立し“ひきこもり”などになりうる心理的リスクが高いプレイヤーは、ゲーム内でも他者との交流を好まない傾向が見られている。同月に弊誌において論文Aを紹介したところ（ 関連記事 ）、当該記事のXにおける ポスト が200万回以上の閲覧を記録するなど、ソーシャルメディアを中心に大きな反響があった。
そこで弊誌では今回、論文Aの執筆者の一人であるブライアン・コンフェッサー氏にメールインタビューを実施。記事への反応として多く見られた「人と関わりたくない」といった声や、「私の事だ」という当事者意識を強く持つ読者の意見を紹介した。くわえて、「ゲームでの出来事やキャラクターとの関係といった“思い出”がどのような役割を持ちうるのか」といったことや、近年急速に進化するAIを用いたデジタルなコミュニケーションについても見解を訊くことができた。
ちなみに、コンフェッサー氏と研究チームは上述した論文Aのほかに、同じ調査対象を別視点で扱った関連論文を7月末に発表している。こちらは「極度の社会的孤立リスクが関連する物語主導、ストラテジー、協力主体のゲームプレイの好み（Extreme social isolation risk is associated with story-driven, strategic and cooperative-first gameplay preferences）」と題され、精神保健分野の国際学術誌「PLOS Mental Health」にて 公開されている （以下、論文B）。今回のインタビューでは、これら2つの論文の違いについても聞いているため、まず論文Bについて軽く触れておきたい。

Blumhouse GamesおよびSolo Gameは9月30日、Perfect Garbageが手がける『Grave Seasons』を2027年3月9日に配信開始すると発表した。日本では時差の関係で3月10日となるようだ。
“殺人鬼とも恋愛できる”ホラー農業シム『Grave Seasons』2027年3月10日配信へ。周回ごとに殺人鬼は変わる、疑心暗鬼な捜査&スローライフ生活
パブリッシャーのBlumhouse GamesおよびSolo Gameは9月30日、Perfect Garbageが手がける『 Grave Seasons 』を2027年3月9日に配信開始すると発表した。日本では時差の関係で3月10日となるようだ。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam/Microsoft Store）/Nintendo Switch/PS5/Xbox Series X|S/XBOX Oneで、Xbox/PC Game Pass向けにも提供される。ゲーム内は日本語表示および字幕に対応予定だ。
『Grave Seasons』は、農業生活と連続殺人事件の調査を組み合わせたホラー農業シミュレーションゲームだ。舞台となるのは、どこか不穏な空気が漂う町「アッシュリッジ」。刑務所から逃げ出した主人公「Dara」はこの町へたどり着き、農業を営みながら新たな生活を始める。しかし町には超自然的な力をもつ連続殺人犯が潜んでおり、住民たちに危険が迫っている。プレイヤーは、穏やかな農業生活を送りつつ、町を脅かす連続殺人犯の謎を暴くのだ。
本作の開発を手がけるPerfect Garbageは、2018年に設立された物語主導型のインディーデベロッパーだ。ホラーやSF、ファンタジーなどを好み、異なるジャンルを組み合わせた作品制作を特徴としている。デビュー作は2023年にリリースされたサイバーパンク・ノワールのビジュアルノベル『Love Shore』で、恋愛要素と怪物や犯罪が絡む物語を描いていた。本作『Grave Seasons』は同デベロッパーの2作目にあたり、今回は農業シミュレーションと超自然的な殺人ミステリーを組み合わせるかたちとなる。農作業の合間に住民の秘密を探り、時には殺人犯との恋愛まで楽しめる本作。その異色の一年がどのように描かれるのか注目される。
『Grave Seasons』は、PC（ Steam / Microsoft Store ）/Nintendo Switch/ PS5 / Xbox Series X|S/XBOX One 向けに2027年3月10日配信予定。Xbox/PC Game Pass向けにも提供される。
本作では、畑を耕して作物を育てるほか、釣りや採掘、採取などをこなしながら一年間を過ごしていく。季節は春夏秋冬の4つに分かれ、45種類以上の種が登場。それぞれ育てられる季節や畑の種類が異なるという。畑についても通常の土壌だけでなく、乾燥地や湿地が用意され、湿地では水やりを必要としない作物なども育てられる。また、収集できるアイテムは600種類以上にのぼり、農場のアップグレードやキャラクターのカスタマイズも可能。料理を作ったり、住民を守るためのオカルトアイテムをクラフトしたりできる。

sources.label: AUTOMATON
sources.evidenceText:
Chobi Softwearは9月25日、戦車戦アクションゲーム『Tank Battle Classic』を配信開始した。
「HPなし」超マニアック戦車アクション『Tank Battle Classic』が注目浴びる。装甲ぶち抜けば“一撃決着”、実戦さながら濃厚砲撃戦
Chobi Softwearは9月25日、戦車戦アクションゲーム『 Tank Battle Classic 』を配信開始した。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam)。“戦車”を題材にマニアックなゲーム開発を続けてきた作者の最新作として、注目を集めている。
『Tank Battle Classic』は第二次世界大戦の戦闘車両を題材にした、シングルプレイヤー向けの戦車アクションゲームだ。プレイヤーはさまざまな戦車を自由に操作し、戦車の性能と地形を活かして敵部隊を撃破する。郊外・市街地・森林・山岳地帯・平原といったマップを舞台に、レトロなビジュアルの戦車戦が繰り広げられる。
そんなモバイル端末向けに活動を続けてきたちょび氏による初のPC向けタイトルが『Tank Battle Classic』だ。本作は記事執筆時点で90件を超えるSteamユーザーレビューを集めており、うち87%の好評とする「非常に好評」のステータスを得ている。操作感はカジュアルで分かりやすく、CPUの敵戦車との戦いには歯ごたえがあるとして、誰でも手に取りやすい本格戦車ゲームとして好評を得ている。特に戦車の動作モーションなどは、戦車マニアからも高い評価を得ている様子だ。今後は新たな戦車やマップの追加も予定されているという。今後のアップデートを通じて、さらなる評価の高まりにも期待したいところだ。
『Tank Battle Classic』はPC向け（ Steam ）に発売中だ。
体当たりハイスピードバトル戦車アクション『SLAM TANK』発表。AI機械たちに砲身大回転攻撃、「砲撃なし」の“肉弾戦車”がゆく
本作での戦車戦は、一般的なヒットポイント制は採用されておらず、砲弾が装甲を貫徹できるかで決着する。戦車の正面は装甲が厚く、逆に側面や背面は弱点となっている。さらに砲弾の威力は距離に応じて低下するうえ、着弾角度も重要になる。斜めに命中させると貫通力が弱まり、跳弾してダメージを与えられない場合があるのだ。つまり戦闘中は敵から垂直の位置を取るように戦車を操縦するのが大事になる。さながら実際の戦車戦のような立ち回りが求められるわけだ。

packages.headline: Diablo 5 Game Director Promises a Return to Methodical Character Builds, but Players Don't Believe Him

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Diablo 5 game director Joe Shely has suggested a return to more methodical gameplay.
Diablo 5 Game Director Promises a Return to Methodical Character Builds, but Players Don't Believe Him
Diablo 5 is still a couple of years away, but that hasn't stopped the speculation on how the game will actually play. People certainly expect a lot of elements from Diablo 3 and 4 to carry over to the new game, but Game Director Joe Shely has suggested a return to more methodical gameplay.
Seemingly in response to the video Path of Exile's Chris Wilson released about Diablo 5 , Shely took to Twitter where he promised "while Diablo 5 will continue to feature some DEX (moment-to-moment execution) mechanics, on balance the game will be an INT/STR game (planning and investment)."
While Diablo V will continue to feature some DEX (moment-to-moment execution) mechanics, on balance the game will be an INT/STR game (planning and investment). We are designing to the core tenet of ARPGs that any challenge can be overcome with the right build.
There has been a lot of discussion around Blizzard invoking Diablo 2 when debuting Diablo 5 at Blizzcon , and how the team needs to shift away from the modern itemization and game design of the last few Diablo games to make that happen. According to Shely's post, it seems like Diablo 5 is heading in that direction. We'll just have to wait and see if Diablo 5's moment-to-moment gameplay is meaningfully different from Diablo 4's focus on infinitely scaling content that you clear in seconds. However, the community seems skeptical.
I've personally never had a problem with Diablo 4's approach to itemization, and I like jumping in and seeing just how far I can push in the Pit each season. But, I also jump back to Diablo and Diablo 2 occasionally when I want to play something that focuses more on creative itemization. Luckily, even if Diablo 5 does lean towards Diablo 2's way of doing things, it sounds like the team will keep adding new seasons to Diablo 4 after launch , so you can always just stick with that game.
Stop me if you've heard this one before.

packages.headline: GTA 5 Modder Taunts Rockstar With Unofficial Nintendo Switch Port, Gets Cease and Desist from Take-Two

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
A modder who was porting GTA 5 to Nintendo Switch taunted Rockstar Games and was immediately hit with a cease and desist.
GTA 5 Modder Taunts Rockstar With Unofficial Nintendo Switch Port, Gets Cease and Desist from Take-Two
The modder, known as Mojso, was planning to bring GTA 5 and GTA Online to Nintendo Switch for modded versions of the console and got a bit cocky. After Rockstar Games recently posted its guidelines for modding (which forbids unofficial ports), the modder posted : "Try me Rockstar, [I don't give a f**k.]"
Three days later, the modder's Discord server was taken down for copyright infringement, but it didn't seem to deter them. After many warned them about how litigous Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two are, the modder suggested they aren't worried about it: "Copyright infringement is anything but enforced in Serbia."
Less than a week later, the modder confirmed they had received a cease and desist from Take-Two Interactive and thanked the company for its "mercy." As a result, the port will never see the light of day, as Mojso has stated that they don't want to risk any legal issues.
When people pointed back to the modder's post about taunting Rockstar, Mojso noted that they didn't actually expect Rockstar to do anything.
"They tried me," Mojso said . "[What the] f**k [do] you want me to do? Fight with them in court? I wasn't expecting them to hit back hard."
The modder had been working on this port using leaked GTA 5 source code, which has resulted in a bevy of other leaks and issues. Ultimately, it's probably in your best interest to not taunt massive corporations that are known for hunting down people that mess with their IP.
"I wasn't expecting them to hit back hard."

Arcade Archives 2 Balloon Bomber will launch for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , and Switch 2 , and Arcade Archives Balloon Bomber for PlayStation 4 and Switch , on October 1, developer Hamster announced . Balloon Bomber is a shooting game released by TAITO in 1980.
Control the anti-aircraft gun and destroy the balloon bombs as they gently sway through the air.
However, destroying the balloon bombs is no easy task. Aim and shoot so your bullets hit only the bomb itself.
If your shot hits the balloon instead, the bomb will fall and blow a hole in the ground. Be careful, as the anti-aircraft gun cannot pass over holes, narrowing your movement range.
The Arcade Archives series is developed with the concept of faithfully reproducing classic arcade games. It also includes convenient features such as difficulty and screen settings, rewind, rapid-fire, and multiple save slots. In addition, players can compete for the best scores with players around the world through online rankings.
Arcade Archives 2 series introduces a brand-new mode called Time Attack Mode, in addition to the Original Mode, Hi Score Mode, and Caravan Mode from Arcade Archives . Time Attack Mode focuses on how quickly you can complete the game, regardless of the score you achieve.
